claim.summary: One-sided density with the Fejer kernel, G(tau) = -int_0^inf h(x) e^{i(x-L) tau} dx, h(x) = x e^{-delta x} P(x - L): int Re G(tau) e^{-i(x-L) tau} d tau = -pi (h(x) + conj h(2L - x)); and if the heights lie in an interval of length c delta and Re G <= S = eps M/delta^2 on the line, then |P(x - L)| <= M (e^{delta x}/(delta x)) ((2/pi)(c eps + 4 sqrt(eps)) + 4 b e^{-b}) for 0 < x <= L.
claim.assessment: Working proof: Fourier inversion for G and its conjugate, the integral of Re G from the value at x = L, and the decay of G away from the heights. The square root comes from the tail 2M/rho and halves the exponent in the theorem that uses it.

formalization.scope: Not formalized; no Lean work assigned.

claim.summary: For P(y) = sum m_j e^{-i y gamma_j} with m_j > 0, M = sum m_j, heights in an interval of length c delta, b = delta L > 1 and 1/b < beta < 1: if log((1 - 1/b)/(1 - beta)) + (1 - beta)/(1 - 1/b) - 1 > pi c, then some x in [1/delta, beta L] has |P(x - L)| > M e^{-beta b} e^{delta x}/(delta x).
claim.assessment: Working proof: the sum is bounded by M in a half-plane and at least M e^{-v c delta} on the imaginary axis; the harmonic majorant of its logarithm, by the mean value inequality for subharmonic functions and Fatou's lemma, as v tends to 0.

formalization.scope: Not formalized; no Lean work assigned.

claim.summary: One-sided density with the Fejer kernel, off-line pairs at one distance delta with heights in an interval of length c delta, c <= 1, b = delta L > 1, 1/b < beta < 1 with log((1 - 1/b)/(1 - beta)) + (1 - beta)/(1 - 1/b) - 1 > pi c: sup Re G >= (pi^2/100)(e^{-beta b} - 4 b e^{-b})_+^2 M/delta^2, so some tau has D_off <= -(2M/(L delta^2))((pi^2/100) e^b (e^{-beta b} - 4 b e^{-b})_+^2 - 3); no dependence on the number of pairs, their gaps or their multiplicities.
claim.assessment: Working proof from the two lemmas. The exponent lost is 2 beta, below 1 only for c < (ln 2 - 1/2)/pi = 0.0615 in the limit of large b; for wider windows the bound gives no negativity, and the hidden binomial family has c about 1.

formalization.scope: Not formalized; no Lean work assigned.

significance.rationale: In the model every cluster confined to a window of height below 0.0615 delta shows in the one-sided density at a bounded multiple of a single pair's length, whatever its size.
significance.next_action: Extend to windows of height delta by removing the square root in the first lemma.

claim.summary: Fejer kernel K_L(w) = 2(1 - cos Lw)/(L w^2), off-line pairs gamma_j -+ i delta with multiplicities m_j, b = delta L: the off-line part of the density sum_z m_z K_L(tau - z) equals -(2 e^b/L) Re G(tau) + E(tau) with G(tau) = sum m_j e^{-iL(tau - gamma_j)}/(tau - gamma_j + i delta)^2, |E| <= 6 Y/L, Y = sum m_j/((tau - gamma_j)^2 + delta^2); G(tau) = -int_0^inf x e^{-delta x} P(x - L) e^{i(x-L) tau} dx with P(y) = sum m_j e^{-iy gamma_j}; and the real points contribute at most (7/3) L N(2 pi/L), N a local count.
claim.assessment: Working proof: the complex cosine split into its growing and decaying exponentials, a Laplace transform identity, and a count of real points by distance in units of 2 pi/L.

claim.summary: One-sided density with the Fejer kernel, n >= 2 off-line pairs at one distance delta with total multiplicity M and height span W, b = delta L >= 3: some x in [1/(2 delta), 2/delta] has |P(x - L)| >= p = M/(2 e b)^n, and J = int_0^inf x^2 e^(-2 delta x) |P(x - L)|^2 dx >= (0.073/delta^2)(p^2/4) min(p/(M W), 3/(4 delta)); no condition on the gaps.
claim.assessment: Working proof from the gap-free power sum bound applied at n sample points. The bound counts every off-line pair of the configuration, not those near one height, and through the earlier constant gives sup Re G only of order (2 e b)^(-6n).

claim.summary: One-sided density with the Fejer kernel, N simple off-line pairs at heights gamma_0 + j pi/L and one distance delta, b = delta L: |P(x - L)| <= 1/cos(pi x/(2L)) for 0 <= x < L and |G(tau)| <= (1 + 3 pi^2/(2 b^2) + N (1 + b/2) e^(-b/2))/delta^2 for all tau, so at this length N = o(e^(b/2)/b) simple pairs give a negative part no larger than 1 + o(1) times one pair's bound.
claim.assessment: Working proof: the exponential sum is a geometric series with ratio -e^(-i pi x/L). An upper bound at the resonant length only.

claim.summary: In the setting of the one-sided density decomposition, with H_jl = 2/(2 delta + i(gamma_j - gamma_l))^3, J = int_0^inf x^2 e^{-2 delta x} |P(x - L)|^2 dx >= lambda_min(H) sum m_j^2 > 0, A1 = pi delta^2 J/M, eps = 2 pi L e^{-b} M and W the span of the heights: sup_tau Re G >= (A1/4 - eps/2)/(W + 16 M/A1); the lower bound for J does not depend on L, so no cluster makes the off-line part of the density nonnegative at arbitrarily large lengths.
claim.assessment: Working proof: Plancherel for G, nonnegativity of the integral of G^2, the integral of G by inversion, and the decay of G away from the heights. The constant is of order J^2 and far from sharp (ratios 10^2 to 10^10 in the control); no lower bound for lambda_min(H) under a local count is obtained.

claim.summary: One-sided density with the Fejer kernel: for k+1 off-line pairs at heights gamma_0 + j pi/L with multiplicities binom(k, j) at one distance delta, |G| <= (k+1)! (pi/b)^k/delta^2 and D_off >= -(2 e^b/(L delta^2)) (k+1)! (pi/b)^k - 6 * 2^k/(L delta^2); with real points on a lattice of spacing s <= 2 pi/L the whole density is nonnegative once 2 pi/s is at least that bound, which for k = floor(b/pi) is at most (2 e^2/(L delta^2)) (b/pi + 1)^(3/2) e^((1 - 1/pi) b) + 6 * 2^(b/pi)/(L delta^2).
claim.assessment: Working proof: the exponential sum is (1 + q)^k with |1 + q| <= pi x/L. With real density l/(2 pi), for each length with b up to about 1.47 log l (asymptotically) the cluster built for that length is hidden at it, where a single pair shows from about log l; its multiplicities are at most l^0.32 there. One cluster per length; not shown that a fixed cluster hides at shorter lengths, that the family shows soon after, or that no admissible cluster hides longer.

formalization.scope: Not formalized; no Lean work assigned.

significance.rationale: In the model a test of the one-sided density at a single length must use a length exceeding the single-pair length by a factor of at least about 1.47, asymptotically, to see every cluster with multiplicities up to the local count; a lower bound only.
significance.next_action: Decide whether a family with bounded multiplicities hides up to lengths of order log T.

claim.summary: For complex z_1..z_N with z_k different from the others, complex b_j and s_nu = sum b_j z_j^nu: for every m >= 0 the maximum of |s_nu| over m < nu <= m + N is at least |b_k| |z_k|^(m+1) times the product over j != k of |z_k - z_j|/(1 + |z_j|). Applied to S(s) = sum m_j (e^{-is w_j^+} + e^{-is w_j^-}) for n off-axis pairs with heights in an interval of length R >= 1: among the points s = nu pi/R, m < nu <= m + 2n, one has |S(s)| >= m_1 e^{(m+1) pi delta_1/R} sinh(pi delta_1/R) times the product over j >= 2 of (2|gamma_1 - gamma_j|/((1+e^{pi/2})R))^2.
claim.assessment: Working elementary proof by Lagrange interpolation. Gives a short range of lattice points (2n of them, step pi/R) where the off-axis sum of a cluster is not small, with a loss that is c^n for evenly spread heights (a power of T for n of order log T) and unbounded for close heights; it carries the exponential at the range's first point and ignores the positivity of multiplicities. Pointwise at lattice points only; not connected to the form's Hilbert-Schmidt norm. Turan's second main theorem, which the queue item names, is unread.

formalization.scope: Not formalized; no Lean work assigned.

significance.rationale: First development of the queued Turan item with a proved substitute: the off-axis sum of a cluster cannot stay small over 2n consecutive lattice points, with a loss governed by the gaps.
significance.next_action: Prove a gap-free bound by Newton interpolation of z^-(m+1) for points of modulus at least one, deduce the cluster consequence, and pass from the lattice point to the mean square.

claim.summary: In the setting of the endpoint moment order with heights in increasing order: k = n-1 if and only if every gap is an odd multiple of pi/Lam and m_j is proportional to the product over l != j of 1/|gamma_j - gamma_l| (the divided-difference weights); if all heights lie in an open interval of length pi/Lam then k = 0.
claim.assessment: Working proof: the solution space of n-1 vanishing moments is spanned by the divided-difference weights, real with alternating signs, and positive multiplicities with unimodular phases match them exactly when consecutive phases are opposite.

claim.summary: For continuous even real g of compact support with phi(s) = Re h(s + i/2) >= 0, h the transform of g: Re h(t+iy) = (1/2pi) int phi(s) K_y(t-s) ds with K_y(t) = 2 pi cos(pi y) cosh(pi t)/(sinh^2(pi t) + cos^2(pi y)); hence Re h(gamma + iy) >= cos(pi y) cos(pi delta) exp(-pi |gamma - gamma0|) Re h(gamma0 + i delta) in the open strip; and if the sum of Re h over a multiset Z of points of the strip is at most B while c Re h(gamma0 + i delta) > B, then cos(pi delta) sum over Z of cos(pi y_rho) exp(-pi |gamma_rho - gamma0|) < c.
claim.assessment: Working elementary proof (Fourier inversion, an explicit Poisson kernel of the strip, Harnack with constants), with a numerical control of the kernel and of the inequality. Limits explicit-formula certificates that require nonnegativity on the whole critical strip: they can exclude a point at distance delta from the line only where the weighted count of actual zeros near its height is below 4/cos(pi delta). The size of that count for zeta is recalled, not derived. Believed classical; no novelty claimed.

formalization.scope: Not formalized; no Lean work assigned.

significance.rationale: Answers the second route review's decisive test: positivity on the whole strip cannot separate a point from the zeros near it, so that formulation reproduces at best the classical region where the zeros nearby are on the line.
significance.next_action: Decide what a certificate needs when positivity is required only outside a window around the height.
